summary: Focused check of the exam card colours plus the existing rank tests. FRONTEND: on the public home page, JEE Main is glossy red (#991B1B) and BITSAT is glossy orange (#C2410C), both with a static reflection gradient. COMEDK is still #101115 with no gradient. The All India banner is still #0B2D80. Checked at 1920x800 and 390x844 in light and dark mode: heading text is white, buttons are readable (#7F1D1D on #FFF1F2, #7C2D12 on #FFEDD5), the page has no horizontal overflow, the ::before sheen has pointer-events:none, hover moves the sheen (translateX goes from -565 to +565 and the card lifts 5px), keyboard focus shows a 3px white outline, and with reduced motion the sheen is hidden (::before display:none). All 9 card links (mocks, chapters, results x 3 exams) work and send a logged-out user to /login?next=/exams/<slug>/<page>. No page errors. BACKEND: ran only the 5 requested rank tests from test_iter105_live_series_isolated.py: 22 of 22 cases passed in 3.5s. The dedicated tejas_isolated_iter105_test DB was dropped afterwards (databases left: admin, config, local, test_database), and the guard checking real DB counts passed. Example rank answers: JEE Main score 150/300 gives estimated rank 22,156-28,132; 268 gives 142-341; 300 gives 1-15; 0 gives 1,222,184-1,390,805. These come from Careers360's 2026 published estimate (secondary_published_estimate, 'not an official' AIR). Scores 269, 270, 20, 25 and 29 fall in gaps in the source table, and -4 and 301 are invalid; all of these return unavailable. COMEDK 175/180 gives 1-10 (Physics Wallah 2025 estimate); 25/180 returns unavailable. BITSAT 300/390 returns unavailable (guidance_only_no_rank_mapping). Attempts that don't match the exam format (retry, preview, corrected, 120 minutes, maximum 240, integer question type, chapter test) all return unavailable. Another student requesting the rank gets 403/404, and a request with no auth gets 401.
critical_code_review_comments: The CSS change is limited to learning-workspace.css lines 15-19. JEE Main and BITSAT share one gradient and sheen rule, and COMEDK has no gradient. The 'stronger hover sheen' comes from a brighter ::before gradient; it reuses the base hover transform and has no separate hover rule, which is fine. The existing reduced-motion rule at line 255 covers it.
seed_data_creation: Only synthetic attempts in the isolated tejas_isolated_iter105_test DB, which was dropped after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rank tests: pytest tests/test_iter105_live_series_isolated.py -k 'test_jee_exact_rows or test_jee_gaps_malformed_out_of_range_unavailable or test_comedk_and_bitsat or test_incompatible_rank_rejected or test_rank_foreign_attempt_denied'. Card testids: exam-home-exam-card-{jee-main,bitsat,comedk}, exam-direct-{mocks,chapters,results}-{slug}. The card element's scrollWidth>clientWidth is expected: overflow:hidden plus the ::before sheen at inset:-60%. Check document-level overflow instead (it is false). The full 71-test series was intentionally not run.
